steps: Independent writers increment their own vector components.
Neither [1,0] nor [0,1] dominates, so the updates are concurrent.
Future comparisons distinguish ancestors from concurrent siblings.

lesson.scenario: Two offline editors update the same document and a merger detects concurrent versions.
entities: Stores the last common document version

steps.title: Common ancestor
steps.outcome: Both copies descend from the same baseline.
steps.invariant: A vector component records knowledge of that participant’s events.

steps.title: A edits offline
steps.narration: Editor A increments its own component to [3,1].
steps.outcome: A version causally descends from the baseline.
steps.invariant: A writer increments only its own component before creating a version.

steps.title: B edits offline
steps.outcome: Neither offline version includes the other edit.
steps.invariant: Vectors x and y are concurrent when neither is component-wise less than or equal to the other.

steps.title: Concurrency detected
steps.narration: The merger compares [3,1] and [2,2] and finds incomparable components.
steps.outcome: The system preserves both siblings for resolution.
steps.invariant: Concurrent versions must not be mistaken for a causal overwrite.

steps.title: Merged descendant
steps.narration: The application merges both fields and emits vector [3,3].
steps.outcome: The merged document causally dominates both inputs.
steps.invariant: A merged vector takes component maxima and advances the merger’s writer component.

production.scenario: A field-service work-order app compares vector clocks from offline tablets and the dispatch web console so concurrent checklist edits are detected before they overwrite each other.
components: Edits the turbine checklist while disconnected at the wind farm
Updates the same work order from headquarters
Determines whether one checklist version descends from another or is concurrent
Authoritative replicated checklist document for the repair job
Attempts automatic field-level merges for concurrent edits
Escalates unresolved conflicts to a dispatcher
flows: The field technician comes back online and uploads local checklist changes with the last vector seen on the device.
Meanwhile the dispatcher has already changed the same work order from the web console.
The sync API compares the tablet and web vectors instead of trusting modified timestamps from two disconnected clients.
When one vector dominates the other, the API writes the newer branch directly into the authoritative work-order store.
If neither vector dominates, the update is classified as concurrent and handed to merge logic instead of being blindly applied.
Automatic merge writes a new checklist version only after both branches are reconciled into one result.
If merge is ambiguous, the supervisor queue gets the two competing branches so a dispatcher can pick the final checklist.
